content:
​President Aleksandar Vučić did not respond to calls for a snap election but instead rallied his supporters. ACLED records over 100 ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) rallies, which the SNS claimed were held against the blockades of traffic and frequent protests. Vučić also accused the protest movement of being funded from “abroad”17 and insulted European parliamentarians from the European Greens faction who had been present at the 8 September rally.18 Although the number of events in September was lower than in August, rallies held by pro- and anti-government groups took place during the last weekend of the month, with clashes occurring in some instances.

title: Protests in Cyprus Demand British Military Bases Out: 'We Don't Want to Be a Launchpad'
content:
Protester Natasha Theodotou told the BBC: "We just want to have an independent Cyprus… Just as we're occupied by the Turkish government in the self-declared Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, recognized only by Ankara, we are occupied by the UK."

The UK retains sovereignty over the Sovereign Base Areas of Akrotiri and Dhekelia under the 1960 Treaty of Establishment, which granted Cyprus independence from British colonial rule. The bases cover about 3% of the island’s territory in the internationally recognised Republic of Cyprus. [...] Demonstrators carried banners reading "Cyprus is not your launchpad" and "British bases out", while chanting "Say it loud, say it clear, British bases out of here". Afoa stated that Cypriots are being put at risk by the ongoing war involving the US, Israel and Iran. "We do not accept Cyprus being a base of war," the group said.

The protest followed a drone strike on RAF Akrotiri on March 1, 2026. The attack, believed to have been carried out by Iran-backed Hezbollah using a Shahed-type drone launched from Lebanon, caused minor damage but no casualties. It was the first direct hit on the base since 1986 and has intensified calls for the UK to end its military presence. [...] RAF Akrotiri supports British Armed Forces operations in Cyprus and the wider region, including reported use by US U-2 spy planes. Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer has authorised "defensive" US actions from the bases against Iranian missile sites. A Ministry of Defence spokesperson said Typhoon and F-35 fighter jets have flown sorties in the region, intercepting Iranian drones and defending civilians from indiscriminate attacks.

title: Anti-war groups plan protests over Cyprus military bases | en.philenews.com
content:
The campaign organisers include Genocide-Free Cyprus, Pancyprian Peace Council, Codepink, Far Right Watch, Palestinian Youth Movement, Peace & Justice Project, Stop the War Coalition, United for Palestine Cyprus, AFOA, Spirithkia, EDON and Proodeftiki.

Historical context

British military presence in Cyprus dates back to 1878 when the United Kingdom received Cyprus as a protectorate from the Ottoman Empire in exchange for the UK’s military support against Russia. When Cyprus gained independence in 1960, the UK retained sovereignty over approximately 98 square miles of territory for military bases at Akrotiri and Dhekelia. [...] RAF Akrotiri, located within Britain’s Sovereign Base Areas in Cyprus, has been used for reconnaissance flights over the eastern Mediterranean since the escalation of conflict in Gaza in October 2023.

The UK government has acknowledged intelligence-sharing arrangements with allied nations but has not detailed specific operations.

Campaign links Cyprus government to military operations

The protest organisers criticised the Cypriot government under President Nikos Christodoulides for facilitating UK and US military operations through access to Cypriot infrastructure.

The campaign demands the dismantling of British Sovereign Base Areas. [...] “Since October 2023, around 600 spy flights have been launched from RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus over Gaza, supplying live intelligence directly to Israel,” the campaign statement said, citing UK official confirmations of intelligence-sharing arrangements.

Protests target UK intelligence operations from Cyprus

Britain has recently shifted surveillance operations from Royal Air Force assets to the Sierra Nevada Corporation, a US defence contractor based in Reno, the protest announcement states.

The company holds full security clearance and operates what activists describe as an extension of US military capabilities.

title: Cyprus peace activists call time on Britain’s bases | New Internationalist
content:
The blast came from the nearby military base, RAF Akrotiri, just a stone’s throw from her home near the city of Limassol on the southern coast of Cyprus. A Shahed-type drone had struck an aircraft hanger in what is believed to have been an attack launched by Hezbollah from Lebanon. In the days that followed, more drones headed towards Cyprus were intercepted, transforming the otherwise idyllic holiday island into a place of fear. Hundreds of locals living near the base like Ifigenia fled their homes, staying in hotels, a nearby monastery or with relatives. 

Although Ifigenia and her family have since returned to Akrotiri, the village on the edge of the base, she says a constant ‘sense of unease’ has lingered: ‘As residents, we bear no responsibility for these conflicts.’ [...] ## Colonial remnants

There have long been demands for Britain to withdraw its RAF bases from Cyprus. In 1960, the island’s struggle against British rule culminated in independence, under a fragile power-sharing arrangement between Greek and Turkish Cypriots. As part of the settlement, Britain retained control over two Sovereign Base Areas. Today, RAF Akrotiri and Dhekelia remain under British jurisdiction and cover three per cent of Cyprus’s land. [...] Advert

As is the case across Cyrpus, people in Limassol, who live with Akrotiri on their doorsteps, are also divided on the bases. Since the attack, Ifigenia explains that some feel reassured by the recent deployment of additional anti-missile systems from Greece and France. Others, particularly those with memories of past conflict, fear the risks of escalation.

For many, the bases are a foreign body and a lingering symbol of colonial rule, says CPC general secretary Charis Pashias: ‘From then until today British military bases in Cyprus are used to implement aggressive imperialist plans and as a launching pad against neighbouring peoples, exposing Cyprus to great dangers as a result.’

# Is the United States Prepared to Defend Cyprus After the Iranian Drone Attack?

## Cyprus Hosts Sovereign British Bases but Exercises No Operational Authority over Their Use

A Royal Air Force Boeing CH-47 Chinook flies over Akrotiri in Cyprus in September 2025.

A Royal Air Force Boeing CH-47 Chinook flies over Akrotiri in Cyprus in September 2025.

Shutterstock [...] Shutterstock

Drone activity near the British base at Akrotiri has moved Cyprus from the margins of the Iran confrontation into its operational perimeter. A drone fell near the base, and authorities intercepted two additional drones heading toward the same area. Security services activated emergency protocols in western Cyprus, temporarily disrupted operations at Paphos Airport, and prompted a public warning from the United States Embassy in Nicosia citing information about a possible drone threat. [...] This exposure also carries implications for London. For the United Kingdom, the incident highlights the dual nature of Akrotiri. The base provides reach into the Eastern Mediterranean and the Levant. Its operational relevance increases during periods of tension. That relevance also increases its visibility to adversaries. Drone attempts allow hostile actors to test defenses and signal capability without crossing into direct confrontation. Even failed attempts place the base within an escalation ladder that shapes future calculations and raises force protection demands.

Drone [activity](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cm2r0q310e3o) near the British base at Akrotiri has moved Cyprus from the margins of the Iran confrontation into its operational perimeter. A drone fell near the base, and authorities intercepted two additional drones heading toward the same area. Security services activated emergency protocols in western Cyprus, temporarily disrupted operations at [Paphos Airport](https://cyprus-mail.com/2026/03/02/paphos-airport-evacuated-reports), and prompted a public [warning](https://cy.usembassy.gov/missile-threat-caution-march-2-2026/) from the United States Embassy in Nicosia citing information about a possible drone threat.

No significant damage occurred; however, the strategic signal is clear: Infrastructure on Cypriot soil that supports Western military posture now sits within demonstrated reach of hostile actors. Cyprus does not want this confrontation, but it no longer can assume insulation from its consequences.

The Republic of Cyprus does not participate as a combatant in the regional confrontation.
